check.name: a failed split or merge changes nothing
long walks reach each node once

title: Split and Merge apply to a copy
body: Both are several steps that can each fail, and replay keeps whatever state an op leaves. Applying them to a clone and swapping it in on success makes them atomic for O(tree) per split or merge, which are rare; every other op validates before it changes anything.

title: A walk's reached set: 32 slots in place, then a bit per slot
body: Allocating a flag per slot made every walk, even one step from a node, cost the graph. Thirty-two reached slots are tracked in place without allocating; past that a bitmap (a 64th of the slot count in words) takes over, which keeps whole-graph walks fast. shortest_path keeps back links in its breadth-first trail instead of an array per slot.
